cover.title:
Kadane's
**algorithm**
cover.lead: The largest sum of numbers in a row: drop the running sum as soon as it goes below zero.
cover.use_it_when: You need the best sum of a subarray (numbers in a row), in one pass.
cover.why_it_matters: It's the first taste of dynamic programming: each step reuses the best answer so far.

slides.title: Watch it run
slides.lead: The largest sum in a row of −2 3 −1 4 −7 5.

slides.title: Carry or drop
slides.scene: A stall carries its running profit from day to day. When the total turns into a loss, it drops it and starts fresh the next day.

blocks.text: A loss carried forward only makes tomorrow [[smaller]], so it gets dropped.

slides.title: Carry or start fresh
slides.lead: Below 0? Start fresh. Then add the number and keep the best.

quickcheck.question: Kadane on 1 −3 2 2 −1. What is the largest sum?

blocks.label: THE RULE
blocks.text: Anything that follows a negative sum is [[bigger without it]]. Starting fresh at 0 is never worse.
So at each number there are only two choices: join the run, or start a new one here.

slides.title: Kadane's algorithm
slides.explain: Lines 5 and 6 drop a negative sum. Line 7 adds the number; line 8 keeps the best.

slides.title: Start best at nums[0]
slides.lead: A subarray needs at least one number. Starting best at 0 invents an empty one.

wrong.note: No real subarray adds up to 0.

cost.note: One pass, two numbers to remember.

problems.title: Maximum Absolute Sum of Any Subarray
problems.note: Use Kadane for the largest and the smallest sum.

blog.summary: The largest sum of numbers in a row: drop the running sum as soon as it goes below zero.
blog.tested_inputs: hand-picked cases (the LeetCode examples, one value, all negative, all zero, values at ±10,000) and random arrays of up to 14 numbers from −10 to 10, plus one array of 3,000 numbers

blog.tested_extra: The running sums, the best sum and the trap result come from running the code.

caption.first: Kadane's algorithm for LeetCode 53 Maximum Subarray: carry a running sum, drop it the moment it goes below zero.
lines: At each number: start fresh if the sum is negative, add, keep the best.
The trap: best = 0 makes −3 −1 −2 return 0 instead of −1.
